finding.claim: update_doc calls can_edit() but ignores its boolean result (should be require_edit), so any user who reaches the route can overwrite any document's body without being owner or editor.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON {"body": ...} for a doc they don't own or edit
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to protected document)

trace.note: update_doc(doc_id) handles PUT with attacker-chosen doc_id
doc = DOCS[doc_id] fetched with no owner scoping
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns bool that is discarded; no abort

finding.guards_checked: can_edit result unused (line 19); require_edit is used correctly only in update_title (line 27), not here; no decorator or before_request auth in the file; g.user is assumed set elsewhere but authorization is not enforced.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool that is discarded at docs.py:19; require_edit (docs.py:11-13), which aborts with 403, is used only in update_title (docs.py:27). The repo has no decorator or before_request hook.
verdict.reason: At docs.py:19 the bare call `can_edit(g.user, doc)` throws away its bool, so docs.py:20 writes the body for any caller who sets g.user, whether or not they are owner or editor. The route decorator sits on line 16 and the def on line 17, a one-line offset that doesn't change the trace.
